dialogues.speaker: Irmgard
dialogues.text: ...Heh. Hafner, you've been wearing a long face for days. Let me guess — you've been agonizing over what gift to get me?

dialogues.speaker: Hafner
dialogues.text: It's just... I wanted to give you something truly worthy of you... especially in front of Mr. Lindemann.

dialogues.speaker: Irmgard
dialogues.text: Worthy of me, or worthy of my father's approval?

dialogues.speaker: Irmgard
dialogues.text: Honestly, Hafner, you're hopeless. If you think a gift alone will convince the old man you're worthy of marrying the heir of the Dornmannshaven family, you'd better start by buying Port Belovodye.

dialogues.speaker: Irmgard
dialogues.text: It really doesn't matter what you give me. As long as it's from you, I'll be happy.

dialogues.speaker: Hafner
dialogues.text: Miss Irmgard... thank you. But I still want to show Mr. Lindemann that his daughter is... in good hands. If I could do that, maybe we wouldn't have to keep sneaking out to see each other...

dialogues.speaker: Irmgard
dialogues.text: Oh, for goodness' sake... you idiot. Honestly, how many times have I told you? If we want to make our relationship public, we can do it anytime. Whatever my father thinks is his business, not ours...

dialogues.speaker: Irmgard
dialogues.text: Anyway, enough about my father. You're on a date with me, not him.

dialogues.speaker: Irmgard
dialogues.text: Look at the moon tonight. It's beautiful. Now tell me, are you going to let me stand here holding this flower all night, or are you going to put it in my hair?
